text:
[LTIM.4.1.1] The runtime must support:

| Expression | Result |
|---|---|
| `Time - Time` | `Duration` |
| `Time + Duration` | `Time` (`tz_offset_ns` of the LHS preserved) |
| `Time - Duration` | `Time` (`tz_offset_ns` of the LHS preserved) |
| `Duration + Duration` | `Duration` |
| `Duration - Duration` | `Duration` |
| `Int * Duration`, `Duration * Int` | `Duration` |
| `Float * Duration`, `Duration * Float` | `Duration` |
| `Duration / Int`, `Duration // Int` | `Duration` (integer division of nanoseconds) |
| `Duration / Float`, `Duration // Float` | `Duration` |
| `Duration % Duration` | `Duration` ([LUNI.8.1]) |
| `Duration / Duration` | `Float` ([LUNI.8.1]) |
| `Duration // Duration` | `Int` ([LUNI.8.1]) |

A `Duration`-valued row whose exact result in nanoseconds is negative yields
`0_s` ([LTIM.1.3.1]): `Time - Time` with the left operand the earlier,
`Duration - Duration` with the right operand the larger, and a product or
quotient with a negative number. How the compiler lowers the saturation is
[RLOW.6.1.6].

A `Duration`-valued row with a `Float` operand takes the `Float` operation over
the nanoseconds ([LEXP.7.3]) and rounds its result, ties to even, to a whole
number of nanoseconds ([LEXP.3.2]). A non-finite result, or one outside `Int`,
raises a `ComputationError` of kind `NOT_REPRESENTABLE` ([LERR.1.4.10]). A zero
divisor is [LEXP.7.15.1]'s. Every other pair of a `Duration` and a number or a
`Duration` is [LUNI.8.3]'s or [LUNI.8.4]'s.

The runtime must evaluate `Time + Duration`, `Time - Duration` and `Time - Time`
exactly. A `Time` result outside the representable range raises as [LTIM.1.1.5]
states. `Time - Time` saturates at any distance between its operands, and a
result greater than $2^{63} - 1$ nanoseconds, which no `Duration` holds, raises a
`ComputationError` of kind `NOT_REPRESENTABLE` ([LERR.1.4.10]), never a wrap.
